DatasetBirth.description: A birth as a dataset records it: the fields `research.study` reads.

altitudeM.description: Metres above sea level; 0 when left out.

instant.description: The instant, a UTC Julian day.

uncertaintyMinutes.description: How far either side the time may be, in minutes; 0 when left out.

utcOffsetSeconds.description: The offset from UTC the birth's clock ran at, seconds east positive.

DatasetRecord.description: One record: a birth, its rating and where it came from.

event.description: The instant of the record's event, a UTC Julian day, for a timed study.

id.description: The record's id, unique in the dataset.

rating.description: How reliable the birth's time is, by its source.

source.description: The source, in words: the register, the book and page, the person.

DatasetStudy.description: One study: the settings it runs under, the worst rating it admits, its groups, and the rest of its request.

groups.description: Each admitted record's group, by its id, for a `COUNTS` or `COMPARE` study.

id.description: The study's id, unique in the dataset.

minimumRating.description: The worst rating the study admits: `AA`, `A`, `B`, `C` or `DD`.

request.description: `research.study`'s request less `births`, `subjects` and `design`, which the dataset supplies.

settings.description: The settings the study is run under, whole.

Hash.description: A SHA-256, as sixty-four hex digits.

Rating.description: How reliable a birth's data is, by its source: the Rodden Rating, as Astro-Databank keeps it (`03-design/receipts-and-datasets.md` §2.1).

oneOf.description: A birth certificate, a civil register or a written family record.
The native, kin or an associate, from memory.
Caution: no source, an ambiguous one, or one not credible.
Dirty data: two or more unsubstantiated, conflicting sources.

SettingsSnapshot.description: The settings something was computed under, whole.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the document's canonical JSON: the `settings_hash` a provenance carries.

profile.description: The profile the settings were resolved from.

settings.description: The settings document, every knob, as `Context::settings_json` writes it, and kept as it was read. Its schema is the settings document's (the MCP server's `settings.describe`), stated there rather than copied here.

records.description: The records, in the order a study reads them.
